Read text_editing.py's copy_source_to_target() directly and found it has exactly 2 policies ('all', 'none') plus an 'invalid' rejection path -- distinct from the already-fully-tested Segment.create_target_from_source(code_policy='copy'|'strip'|'empty'). 2. Read the 'none' branch's exact behavior (target_attributes filtered to only xml:space, xml:lang never copied unless target_language explicitly passed) and wrote 4 tests proving the plain-text-only structure, the xml:space/xml:lang asymmetry, explicit target_language handling, and a direct 'all' vs 'none' structural comparison.

Checked whether attribute-inheritance resolution (the rule_text's 'inherited attributes resolved' clause) exists at all, not just whether it's tested -- grepped model/document.py for inherit/effective_/resolved_ and found nothing. Confirmed this is a genuine, unbuilt gap: each typed class stores only its own local attributes dict; nothing walks ancestors to resolve an effective xml:space/xml:lang for a descendant that doesn't declare it locally. Recorded both XLIFF-MODEL-001 obligations as honestly partial with this precise reason rather than force-promoted to implemented.
